title: Flood Appraisal Loading Against the Summit Loan's Closing Value
content:
Desk note for Set-Aside Accounts — Summit Tax and Insurance Reserve, flood reviews.

*Which appraisal counts?* An appraisal carried by the loan's maturity case (Maturity and Due-and-Payable Cases) that is due and payable or in its extension period, dated fewer whole calendar months before the review than the appraisal-currency months, 6. It is compared with the Summit loan's appraised value at closing (Cedarline Summit Proprietary Reverse Mortgage).

*What loading follows?*
- Appraised value above the closing value by more than the appraisal threshold percentage, 10.0 percent: the high appraisal loading, 6.0 percent.
- Above the closing value by no more than that threshold: the low appraisal loading, 3.0 percent.
- Otherwise — no such appraisal, or a value not above the closing value: no appraisal loading under this rule.

*Hypothetical:* closing value 250,000.00, so the threshold point is 275,000.00. A 4-month-old case appraisal of 280,000.00 gives 6.0 percent; one of 260,000.00 gives 3.0 percent; a 7-month-old appraisal of 280,000.00 gives none.
